items.title: The reduction of a formal completion is the reduced closed subspace it is taken along
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For an algebraic space X and a closed subset T, the lemma asserts that the reduction of the completion of X along T is the reduced induced closed subspace corresponding to T (statement lines 3254-3261). The proof does not compute with the construction of the completion but compares universal properties: it cites the description of the reduction of a formal algebraic space, the definition of the reduced induced closed subspace and the definition of the completion, and observes that both sides are reduced algebraic spaces characterised by the same mapping property, namely that a morphism from a reduced algebraic space factors through them exactly when its image lies in T (proof lines 3263-3273). The claim is H2: the argument is short but it is a complete identification of two objects by their universal properties, and each of the three inputs is named.
